extract_student_records.description: Retrieve a student's academic record by roll number, searched from indexed institutional spreadsheets.
extract_student_records.limitations: Requires a roll number stated in the request and the indexed spreadsheet directory to be present; honestly reports 'not found' or 'records unavailable' rather than returning simulated data.

fetch_drive_spreadsheet.description: Read rows from a Google Sheets spreadsheet by spreadsheet ID and range.
fetch_drive_spreadsheet.limitations: No Google service-account credentials are configured at uri_workspace/credentials.json; reports 'unavailable' honestly rather than returning simulated data until they are.

draft_institutional_note.description: Draft an institutional office note/noting: the Brain composes the body from the request's purpose, the institution's configured conventions, the operating policy's drafting rules, and any attached-file evidence. Structure adapts to purpose; not a fixed template.
draft_institutional_note.limitations: Drafting only; does not submit, approve, or file the noting anywhere.

draft_institutional_order.description: Draft an institutional office order: the Brain composes the body from the request's purpose (e.g. appointment, cancellation, delegation), the institution's configured conventions, the operating policy's drafting rules, and any attached-file evidence. Structure adapts to purpose; not a fixed template.
draft_institutional_order.limitations: Drafting only; does not issue, sign, or distribute the order.

generate_document.description: Generate a real Office file (DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, or PDF) for a general request that is not an institutional note or order - the Brain composes the content (reusing the same policy/evidence/institutional-conventions assembly as note/order drafting); the requested file format is detected from the request and rendered into a real, downloadable file. Not a fixed template.
generate_document.limitations: Generation only; does not distribute, upload, or file the document anywhere. PDF output is plain-text pagination, not rich layout.

system_performance.description: Report the current PC's real CPU, memory, swap, and disk usage - a live read-only snapshot, never estimated.
system_performance.limitations: Read-only reporting; does not configure, throttle, or terminate anything.

remember_fact.description: Save a fact the user explicitly asked URI to remember or add to their profile (e.g. their workplace, a stated preference) - never triggered by an incidental mention, only an explicit save/remember request.
remember_fact.limitations: Only ever writes with consent='user_provided' (the user's own explicit request) - never guesses or auto-captures from ordinary conversation.

recall_memory.description: Answer a question about what URI already remembers about the user (name, stated preferences, prior context) from their own confirmed memory entries - never invents an answer if nothing relevant is saved.
recall_memory.limitations: Only reads already-consented (user_provided/user_confirmed) memory entries; never writes new memory itself.

convert_document.description: Convert an already-attached document into a different file format - today, an attached PDF into a real DOCX, using its actual extracted text (OCR fallback for scanned pages).
convert_document.limitations: PDF-to-DOCX only today; requires the source PDF already attached to this conversation.

read_attached_file.description: Read the text of a current-turn attachment the user attached to this conversation (PDF including scanned/OCR, plain text, CSV, JSON, spreadsheet, image, or Word document), returning the extracted text as evidence for the Brain to reason from - never an answer URI composes itself.
read_attached_file.limitations: Reads only files the user actually attached to the current conversation; honestly reports when nothing is attached, when a file type has no text extractor, when a document contains no readable text, or when extraction fails, rather than inventing content.

gmail_search.description: Search the user's Gmail for messages matching an administrative query, returning subject/date/snippet as evidence for the Brain to reason from - never an answer URI composes itself.
gmail_search.limitations: Requires uri_workspace/credentials.json (a Google OAuth client secret) and a completed one-time OAuth consent; honestly reports when credentials are missing, authentication fails, or the search returns no results rather than inventing information.

gmail_find_draft.description: Search the user's existing Gmail drafts (read-only) for one relevant to the request, returning it as evidence for the Brain to reason from. URI cannot create, modify, send, or delete drafts through this capability.
gmail_find_draft.limitations: Requires the same Google OAuth credentials as gmail_search; reports 'not found' when Gmail is unavailable or when no relevant draft exists, and cannot distinguish those two cases from the underlying service's return value.

web_search.description: Search the public Internet for real, current information via a real search API, returning titles/URLs/content snippets as evidence for the Brain to reason from - never an answer URI composes itself.
web_search.limitations: Requires a configured TAVILY_API_KEY (see .env.example); honestly reports when the search service is unreachable, misconfigured, or returns no results rather than inventing information.

drive_search.description: Search Google Drive (files the user already has access to) by name/content and return real file metadata (id, name, type) as evidence - read-only, the same scope Gmail/Drive already share.
drive_search.limitations: Requires a stored Google OAuth token (token.json) on the server host; honestly reports 'unavailable' with the real reason when Drive is not connected rather than inventing results.

gmail_create_draft.description: Create a Gmail DRAFT (never sends it) - the Brain composes the subject/body from the request and any evidence; the recipient is taken directly from an email address in the request text. The user still reviews and sends the draft themselves in Gmail.
gmail_create_draft.limitations: Requires a stored Google OAuth token with gmail.compose scope on the server host; creates a draft only - there is no capability anywhere in URI that sends an email.

drive_upload.description: Upload the most recently generated or attached file in this conversation to Google Drive as a new file - never overwrites, moves, renames, or deletes anything already in Drive.
drive_upload.limitations: Requires a stored Google OAuth token with drive.file scope on the server host, and a file already generated or attached in this conversation to upload.

google_workspace_create.description: Create a new Google Drive folder, professionally formatted Google Sheet with headers and blank rows, Google Doc, Slides presentation, or text-question Form. Optionally place it in an exact-name visible folder, creating that folder if absent. Requires user approval before any write; never changes existing files. Use this for requests to create a Google file in Drive.
google_workspace_create.limitations: Requires per-user Google sign-in with drive.file scope and the relevant Google API enabled. A same-name file in the target folder is reported instead of duplicated.

fetch_url.description: Fetch one web page or document by URL and extract its readable text as evidence (HTML, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, plain text, CSV) - lets URI actually read a source web_search found (or one the user gave directly), not just cite its search-result snippet.
fetch_url.limitations: The URL must appear literally in the request text (the Brain cannot supply an arbitrary URL of its own choosing - see the tool's own module docstring on the argument boundary); bounded to 10 MB and content types URI can extract text from; honestly reports an unreachable page, an unsupported content type, or an empty result rather than inventing content.

pc_system_optimization.description: Inspect and optimize this device's performance (e.g. startup programs, disk/temp cleanup, resource-heavy processes) with explicit user approval before any change.
pc_system_optimization.limitations: No execution adapter exists yet; this entry exists so URI can explain the gap honestly rather than pretend the capability is available. See the Controlled Self-Development architecture (research -> propose -> approve -> test -> approve -> execute -> verify -> rollback) for how this would eventually be built - none of that pipeline exists yet either.
